Arthur Conan Doyle, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/arthur-conan-doyle/the-adventures-of-sherlock-holmes

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Arthur Conan Doyle, the author, died 1930.

First publication of the text used: July 1891, in The Strand Magazine (United Kingdom), in monthly issues from July 1891 to June 1892 (Wikipedia). The book followed on 14 October 1892 (George Newnes, United Kingdom). SE colophon: 'The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes was published in 1892 by Arthur Conan Doyle.'

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1891, before 1931, so it is in the public domain in the United States.
- Country of origin: copyright lasts for life plus 70 years after the death of the last person named above. The last to die did so in 1930, so the work entered the public domain there on 1 January 2001. The first publication (July 1891) was in the United Kingdom.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
